title: Give every train both a registry entry and a spec file

facts.note: Any creation, edit, rename or deletion of the train registry or a train spec file is visible from changed paths; existing files are visible for whole-repo validation.

values: train registry entry added, renamed, removed, moved or edited
registry theme-category group added, renamed, removed or reordered
train spec file added, renamed, deleted or edited
registry entry outside a nominal/error/alternate/exception group
facts.note: Requires comparing train_ids in plan/_trains.yaml with files under plan/_trains/, and parsing the registry's theme-category grouping, for both changed and pre-existing trains.
The planner phase gate is where the validator enforces the rule; it does not limit the invariant, which holds for every train at all times.
Task wording indicating trains are being planned, changed, regrouped or reviewed; path and change facts remain the deterministic triggers.

fires: A new train entry is added to plan/_trains.yaml.
A train_id is renamed in the registry, or an existing train entry's contents are updated.
A registry entry is moved between theme-category groups, or a group in plan/_trains.yaml is added, renamed, removed or reordered.
A file under plan/_trains/ is created, renamed, deleted or edited.
A spec file exists under plan/_trains/ with no corresponding registry entry.
Validating or reviewing existing trains, including pre-existing registry entries whose spec file is missing or that sit outside a nominal/error/alternate/exception group.
doesNotFire: Planning work that touches only wagon, feature or acceptance files and leaves plan/_trains.yaml and plan/_trains/ untouched, while every existing train already has a registry entry in a valid theme-category group and a matching spec file.
Source or test changes that modify no planning artifacts, while the train registry is correctly theme-category-grouped and every registry entry is paired with its spec file.

given: plan/_trains.yaml is the train registry, grouped by theme category; plan/_trains/ holds one spec file per train.
when: You add, change, rename, regroup, remove or validate any train, registry entry or train spec file.
then: Ensure every train has both a registry entry in plan/_trains.yaml and a full spec at plan/_trains/{train_id}.yaml, so every registry entry has its spec file.
prefer: Two-file pattern: registry entry (train_id, description, path, wagons summary) plus spec file (full workflow).
Create the spec file in the same change as the registry entry, named from the train_id.
Place each registry entry under its theme-category group: nominal, error, alternate or exception.
avoid: A registry entry without its spec file, including a stale entry left after the spec is renamed or deleted.
A spec file under plan/_trains/ with no registry entry.
Spec filenames that do not match the registry train_id.
why: Each train needs both files; validator SPEC-TRAIN-VAL-0003 fails the planner phase gate when a spec file is missing.
evidence: For each train_id in plan/_trains.yaml, plan/_trains/{train_id}.yaml exists, and each train spec file has a registry entry.
Validator SPEC-TRAIN-VAL-0003 passes; the planner phase gate fails if any spec file is missing.
Every registry entry sits under one of the theme-category groups nominal, error, alternate, exception.
verifier_detail: Validator SPEC-TRAIN-VAL-0003: enumerate registry entries in plan/_trains.yaml and fail the planner phase gate for each entry whose plan/_trains/{train_id}.yaml spec file is missing.

Registry layout is theme-category-grouped: nominal, error, alternate, exception. Until a separate grouping convention (proposed planner.train.registry-grouping) is active, this rule's activation also covers grouping changes and misgrouped entries.
Registry entry fields: train_id, description, path, wagons summary. Spec file holds the full workflow.
Term two_file_pattern = registry entry + spec file per train; values registry: plan/_trains.yaml, spec: plan/_trains/{train_id}.yaml.
Severity 3; disposition strict (as declared in source metadata).

additions.text: Theme-category grouping (S009) is an independently violable obligation and should become its own convention planner.train.registry-grouping. Until that convention exists and is active, this rule retains the grouping requirement in prefer[2], evidence[2] and verifier_detail[1], and its activation fires on grouping changes and misgrouped entries; doesNotFire cases require both valid pairing and valid grouping.
additions.justification: Rule 2 plus auditor fix: then carries only the pairing obligation, but grouping must not lose activation coverage.

additions.justification: Direct negations of 'each train needs two files' (S006) and the {train_id} filename template (S019).
